title: Why Is Your Ice Cloudy in the Middle? #science #ice
description:
The cloud in your ice is mostly trapped air. Tap water holds dissolved air, but ice can hold very little. An ice tray freezes from the outside in, pushing the air toward the middle. The last water to freeze is packed with air, so tiny bubbles form and get locked in. Freeze water from one side only (an insulated box, cold from the top) and the air is pushed into the last layer: cut that off, and the rest of the ice is clear.

More about heat: Why does metal feel colder than wood? (long video on the channel)

Sources
